 --> Gold prices fall Rs 3,200 to 10-month low in Delhi; silver down Rs 4,200
 Gold prices in Delhi fell Rs 3,200 to a 10-month low of Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, while silver declined Rs 4,200 per kg, tracking a sharp global sell-off amid inflation and interest rate concerns. 
 Moneycontrol News 
 October 31, 2026 / 20:11 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Gold, silver extend losses as global sell-off deepens; gold hits 10-month low 
 Gold prices in the national capital fell Rs 3,200 to a 10-month low of Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams on Saturday, extending losses for a second consecutive session amid a sharp global sell-off in precious metals.
 The yellow metal of 99.9% purity declined to Rs 1,42,000 per 10 grams, inclusive of all taxes, from Friday's close of Rs 1,45,200 per 10 grams, according to the All India Sarafa Association.
 It was last quoted at Rs 1,42,300 per 10 grams on December 26, 2025.
 Silver prices also continued their downward trajectory, falling Rs 4,200 to Rs 1,86,000 per kilogram, inclusive of all taxes, from the previous close of Rs 1,90,200 per kg.
 The white metal was last trading around these levels on December 8, 2025, when it was quoted at Rs 1,85,000 per kg.

 U.S. Fed Holds Interest Rates Steady, Warsh Says Economy Not Running Too Hot 
 "Gold and silver prices were weighed down by rising energy prices, which fuelled inflation concerns, and hawkish commentary from the US Federal Reserve," said Rahul Khetawat, senior vice-president and fund manager at 360 ONE Asset.
 These developments tempered expectations of monetary easing and put pressure on precious metals, leading to a correction in prices, he said.
 In overseas markets, spot gold plunged $145.84, or nearly 4%, to close at $3,875.55 per ounce on Friday, hitting its lowest level in more than a year. It was last quoted around this level at $3,887.09 per ounce on October 3, 2025.
 Spot silver also tumbled $3.04, or 6%, to settle at $49.12 per ounce. The metal was last quoted at $48.02 per ounce on November 6, 2025.
 "Gold fell towards $3,800 and silver slipped below $50 per ounce, while Shanghai contracts also dropped sharply while still at a premium to global markets, especially for the white metal," said Manav Modi, commodities analyst at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.
 He added that higher oil prices and firm inflation had revived expectations of a December Fed rate hike, strengthening the case for higher-for-longer interest rates by the US Federal Reserve.
 Modi also pointed out that an AI-led equity market rout added to forced liquidation and cash-raising pressure, while silver's industrial exposure amplified its fall. In China, reports of investors selling gold to raise cash were a possible additional factor, though this was not confirmed.
 He noted that speculative short positions had also built up ahead of the US midterm elections, with President Donald Trump's majority likely to be an important factor in determining the further trajectory of bullion prices.
 (With PTI inputs)
